title: Check where sail reads every record twice to name an index
body:
`libsail` has two ways to give an index its names.

- `Index::build_named(bytes, format)` reads the file once and keeps each record's offset and name as it goes.
- `name_index()` runs on a collection that is already open: `IndexedFasta`, `IndexedStockholm` or `IndexedHmm`. It reads every record's bytes a second time through `Source::range`, one read per record, to find the names.

`sail index` takes the second route. It calls `IndexedFasta::open`, which scans the file for offsets, then calls `name_index()`, which reads every record again (`commands/index.rs:46`, and the same in the Stockholm and HMM arms). `sail names` already takes the first route when the index file has no names (`commands/names.rs:97`).

## Proposal

Go through each place where `sail` builds or opens an index, and decide whether a single pass would do. A place qualifies only when it builds the index itself and then needs the names. Jack expects most places to stay as they are, and a few to change. A place that stays gets a note here saying why. A place that changes gets a commit on `dev`. Neither outcome touches `libsail`'s API or `sail`'s command line.

| place | how it gets an index | whether it reads names |
|---|---|---|
| `commands/index.rs` | `IndexedX::open`, then `name_index()` | yes, written to the index file |
| `commands/names.rs` | the index file, or `build_named` when that has no names | yes, printed |
| `commands/count.rs` | `Index::build` | no |
| `input::index_of` | the current index file, or `Index::build` | through the command that called it |
| `commands/dedup.rs`, `commands/fetch.rs` | `index_of` on the indexed backend | yes, from each record with `seq::name_of` |
| `commands/validate.rs` | `IndexedX::open` | not checked |

## Out of scope

Whether naming should report repeated names is sail-c04fbf.
